subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which type of force tends to stretch or pull a material apart?
questions.explain: Tension is a pulling force that stretches a material and tries to pull it apart.

questions.q: Which force squashes or pushes a material together, tending to shorten it?
questions.explain: Compression is a pushing force that squashes a material and tends to shorten or crush it.

questions.q: Shear force is best described as two forces acting in which way?
options: In opposite directions across a material, tending to make it slide or cut
Pulling directly apart along the same line
Pushing directly together along the same line
questions.explain: Shear occurs when opposing forces act across a material, causing one part to slide relative to another.

questions.q: During a tug of war, the rope between the two teams is mainly experiencing which force?
questions.explain: The teams pull in opposite directions, stretching the rope and placing it in tension.

questions.q: A vertical column supporting the weight of a roof is mainly in which state?
questions.explain: The roof load pushes down on the column, squashing it, so the column is in compression.

questions.q: When a pair of scissors cuts through paper, which force is applied to the paper?
questions.explain: The two blades push past each other in opposite directions, applying a shear force that cuts the paper.

questions.q: A structural member that is designed to resist a compression force is called a:
questions.explain: A strut is a member that carries compression (pushing) forces.

questions.q: A structural member that is designed to resist a tension force is called a:
questions.explain: A tie is a member that carries tension (pulling) forces.

questions.q: Which structural member is a horizontal element that spans a gap and carries loads across it?
questions.explain: A beam is a horizontal member that spans between supports and carries loads across a gap.

questions.q: Which combination makes a structure most stable and least likely to topple?
options: A wide base and a low centre of gravity
A narrow base and a high centre of gravity
A wide base and a high centre of gravity
A narrow base and a low centre of gravity
questions.explain: A wide base and low centre of gravity keep the line of action of the weight within the base, improving stability.

questions.q: A cantilever is best described as a beam that is:
options: Fixed and supported at one end only, with the other end projecting freely
Held in tension by cables at each end
Free to rotate at both ends
questions.explain: A cantilever is rigidly fixed at one end while the other end projects out unsupported.

questions.q: A designer wants a table lamp that is hard to knock over. Which design feature would best improve its stability?
options: A heavy, wide base and keeping most of the weight low down
A tall, narrow stem with the bulb weight at the top
A lightweight base with a high centre of gravity
A rounded base so it can rock freely
questions.explain: A heavy wide base with weight low down lowers the centre of gravity and widens the base, resisting toppling.

questions.q: Which two-dimensional shape is naturally the most rigid and is used in triangulation?
questions.explain: A triangle cannot change shape without changing the length of a side, making it the most rigid frame shape.

questions.q: Why does adding triangulation to a rectangular frame make it more rigid?
options: The triangle formed cannot be distorted without changing the length of its members
It adds extra weight that holds the frame down
It allows the joints to rotate more freely
It changes tension in the frame into shear
questions.explain: Triangulation braces the frame into triangles, which are rigid because their shape is fixed by the member lengths.

questions.q: Steel reinforcing bars are added to concrete mainly because concrete is weak in:
questions.explain: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension, so steel bars are added to carry the tensile forces.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a gusset plate at a joint in a framework?
options: To strengthen and stiffen the joint where members meet
To allow the members to slide past each other
To add decoration to the structure
To reduce the overall weight of the frame
questions.explain: A gusset plate spreads the load over a joint and reinforces it, making the connection stronger and stiffer.

questions.q: A rectangular wooden frame racks (leans) sideways under load. What is the simplest way to make it rigid?
options: Fit a diagonal member to triangulate the frame
Make all four members thicker but keep it rectangular
Round off the corners of the frame
Add weight to the top of the frame
questions.explain: A diagonal brace divides the rectangle into rigid triangles, preventing it from racking.

questions.q: Corrugating a flat sheet of material (giving it a wavy cross-section) mainly increases its:
questions.explain: Corrugation increases the depth of the cross-section, greatly improving stiffness and resistance to bending.

questions.q: When a horizontal beam bends under a load applied to its top, which forces act within it?
options: Compression on the top surface and tension on the bottom surface
Tension on the top surface and shear on the bottom surface
questions.explain: Bending squashes the upper fibres (compression) and stretches the lower fibres (tension) of the beam.

questions.q: A tall, thin display stand keeps tipping over easily. Which change would most improve its stability?
options: Widen the base and move heavy components lower down
Make it taller so it is easier to see
Move the heaviest components to the top
Make the base narrower to save material
questions.explain: Widening the base and lowering the mass reduces the centre of gravity, making the stand far less likely to tip.
